question.:question/problem: Find $(u(t)f(t))^{′}$ where $f(t)=\begin{bmatrix}- 3 t - 3 \\ - 3 e^{t} \\ - 3 t^{3}\end{bmatrix}$ and $u(t)=t^{2}.$
question.:question/worked-solution:
Using the scalar function multiple rule, we can write

$$
(u(t)f(t))^{′}=u^{′}(t)f(t)+u(t)f^{′}(t).
$$

Let's find $u^{′}(t)$ and $f^{′}(t).$

$$
\begin{aligned}f^{′}(t)&=\begin{bmatrix}\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(- 3 t - 3) \\ \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(- 3 e^{t}) \\ \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(- 3 t^{3})\end{bmatrix}=\begin{bmatrix}-3 \\ - 3 e^{t} \\ - 9 t^{2}\end{bmatrix}\\u^{′}(t)&=\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(t^{2})=2 t\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we obtain:

$$
\begin{aligned}(u(t)f(t))^{′}&=u^{′}(t)f(t)+u(t)f^{′}(t)\\&=(2 t)\begin{bmatrix}- 3 t - 3 \\ - 3 e^{t} \\ - 3 t^{3}\end{bmatrix}+(t^{2})\begin{bmatrix}-3 \\ - 3 e^{t} \\ - 9 t^{2}\end{bmatrix}\\&=\begin{bmatrix}2 t \left(- 3 t - 3\right) \\ - 6 t e^{t} \\ - 6 t^{4}\end{bmatrix}+\begin{bmatrix}- 3 t^{2} \\ - 3 t^{2} e^{t} \\ - 9 t^{4}\end{bmatrix}\\&=\begin{bmatrix}3 t \left(- 3 t - 2\right) \\ 3 t \left(- t - 2\right) e^{t} \\ - 15 t^{4}\end{bmatrix}\end{aligned}
$$

:answer-field/choices.:answer/value: \begin{bmatrix}- 6 t^{2} - 6 t \\ - 6 t e^{t} \\ - 6 t^{4}\end{bmatrix}
\begin{bmatrix}- 3 t^{2} \\ - 3 t^{2} e^{t} \\ - 9 t^{4}\end{bmatrix}
\begin{bmatrix}- 9 t^{2} - 6 t \\ - 3 t^{2} e^{t} - 6 t e^{t} \\ - 15 t^{4}\end{bmatrix}
\begin{bmatrix}- 6 t \\ - 6 t e^{t} \\ - 18 t^{3}\end{bmatrix}
